verdict.root_cause: A platform-automation traffic-shaping sidecar was attached to product-catalog's network namespace ~4 minutes before onset, applying a fixed 300ms/zero-jitter egress delay on eth0, still in place at onset with no matching removal [tr_b45878409cfe]. Every caller span into product-catalog carries a matching ~300-305ms of client-side self-time sitting on the response/egress leg, with server spans opening only 1-2ms after their client parent [tr_e5c454946a85]. product-catalog returns no errors at all across incident and baseline [tr_7a4c7ba2e4cc, tr_8497562b82fa], so this is a pure latency event: frontend, recommendation and the other alerting services failed because they waited, with four concurrent GetProduct calls serializing to ~2.7s on the recommendations route.
verdict.reasoning: The change log gives a latency-injecting state transition on product-catalog at 08:13:04, the only change in the window, with no deploy, config edit or flag flip [tr_b45878409cfe]. The traces show exactly the signature that change predicts: a flat, jitter-free ~300ms on the caller side of every product-catalog edge, consumed after the server returns rather than at call setup [tr_e5c454946a85]. Metrics show error ratio flat at zero with zero variance over 488 samples, identical to baseline, with continuous coverage proving the service alive — ruling out an error-propagation origin and ruling out the sidecar having broken the request path outright [tr_7a4c7ba2e4cc, tr_8497562b82fa]. Callers are waiting, not failing, which matches checkout alerting a minute later on deadlines. I blame product-catalog rather than frontend because frontend's own handler spans are sub-2ms and frontend-proxy passes through at 0.1-1.1ms [tr_e5c454946a85]. The fix is removing the injected shaping, not a rollback or restart, since no artifact changed. Confidence is medium because the 300ms explains only about a third of fast-path latency.
open_questions: No latency percentiles or request rates were ever returned — both metric dispatches came back as error-ratio templates [tr_7a4c7ba2e4cc, tr_8497562b82fa], so the 300ms step is inferred from ten traces, not confirmed against product-catalog's own p50/p95/p99.

The ~600ms sql.conn.query leg and the 1.2-1.5s of handler self-time before the query is issued in half the traces [tr_e5c454946a85] are unexplained by a 300ms egress delay — queuing backpressure, pool saturation, or an independently slow datastore are all still open.

All sampled traces cluster between 08:13:16 and 08:15:57 with none near the 08:17:31 onset [tr_e5c454946a85]; Loki returned zero lines for both product-catalog and frontend across the whole window [tr_8b64d2581ea0, tr_c7ae3b3db44f], so no self-reported evidence exists and all sources are untrusted and uncorroborated.

alternatives.root_cause: product-catalog is exhausting an internal resource (connection pool or worker threads), queuing requests 1.2-1.5s in-process before issuing the DB call, with the sidecar delay incidental.
alternatives.why_not: The long handler self-time appears in only about half the traces and is plausibly downstream of the injected delay, since concurrent GetProduct calls are observed serializing [tr_e5c454946a85]; no pool, thread or memory metric was collected and no change lowered a limit [tr_b45878409cfe], while the 300ms matches a recorded change in magnitude, shape and timing.

alternatives.root_cause: product-catalog's database degraded independently and the ~600ms sql.conn.query leg is the true origin of user-visible latency.
alternatives.why_not: No baseline for the DB leg was obtained, so that cost may be normal for this path; no change touched the datastore [tr_b45878409cfe], and it cannot explain the ~300ms sitting outside the server span nor the onset timing tracking the sidecar attach [tr_e5c454946a85].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no effect should be observed. The effect that would resolve this incident — removal of the 300ms/0-jitter netem delay on eth0 in product-catalog's network namespace — is not reachable by any available action, and would show up as frontend's GetProduct client-span self-time dropping from ~300-305ms to ~1-5ms and the recommendations route root latency falling from ~2.7s toward ~1s.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the executor can in fact reach the shaping sidecar. Two concrete checks would overturn it: (a) change-log shows a prior recorded *configuration* for product-catalog whose revert also detaches the traffic-shaping container — the current record explicitly shows no config-change events and only namespace attach/remove entries [tr_b45878409cfe]; or (b) recreating product-catalog's container is confirmed to tear down the shared network namespace and with it the netem qdisc, in which case restart_service becomes a candidate. It is also wrong if the latency is in fact process-state-resident in product-catalog rather than in the namespace — but the trace evidence puts ~300ms on the response/egress leg after the server span closes [tr_e5c454946a85], which a process restart would not address, and the ~600ms sql.conn.query leg plus 1.2-1.5s of pre-query handler self-time in half the traces [tr_e5c454946a85] remain unexplained by either mechanism.
proposal.risk: Abstaining is not free: the shaping sidecar is still attached with no matching removal [tr_b45878409cfe], so the latency persists and frontend, recommendation, checkout and load-generator keep alerting until a human detaches it. The risk I am declining to take is the larger one — revert_config on product-catalog has an unmet precondition (the change history explicitly records no configuration change for this service in the window [tr_b45878409cfe]), so it would restore some unrelated prior environment, recreate the container, and almost certainly leave the netem delay in place while adding a connection reset and a cache flush on a service that is currently serving every request successfully [tr_8497562b82fa]. rollback_image is equally unmet: no deploy or image change appears in the window. restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and the evidence points squarely at an external change. Acting on any of the three would be a change to a service with a zero error ratio, on a diagnosis the metrics never confirmed — no p50/p95/p99 or request-rate series was ever returned [tr_7a4c7ba2e4cc, tr_8497562b82fa], so the 300ms step is inferred from ten traces that all predate onset by 90 seconds to 4 minutes [tr_e5c454946a85].
proposal.blast_radius: No services are touched by this abstention. Had an action been taken on product-catalog, the inbound edges that would have seen the container recreate are frontend (both /api/products/{productId} and /api/recommendations routes) and recommendation via get_product_list -> ListProducts [tr_e5c454946a85], and transitively frontend-proxy and load-generator at the edge; checkout appears in the blast radius but no checkout span touches product-catalog in any sampled trace [tr_e5c454946a85]. The escalation this proposal implies — manual detach of the platform-automation traffic-shaping container — has the same reach, plus whatever scheduled job owns the attach/remove cycle, which will re-attach on its next pass unless it is stopped.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Six services alerted simultaneously across frontend, catalog, recommendation and then checkout, which is far more than a single-service warning and cannot be dismissed. The shared fan-out suggests a common downstream or config/flag dependency, but nothing in the alerts pins a class yet.
